parsed.rationale: Although both records are `type-alias-object` kinds with `shared_field_count: 2` and neither is test, codegen, mock, or sample-app code, they carry distinct names (`PauseWXYC` in `Shared/Intents/Sources/Intents/PauseWXYC.swift` vs. `WhatsPlayingOnWXYC` in `WXYC/iOS/Intents.swift`) that strongly suggest they alias different underlying Siri/App Intents types representing semantically unrelated user actions — pausing playback versus querying what is currently playing. The structural similarity (both are empty-field type aliases) is a coincidence of the Intents framework pattern, not a sign of copy-paste duplication. Merging or extracting them would conflate two distinct intent definitions and break the intent-handler dispatch that depends on each name.
